domain_reasoning: Most time goes into drafting scripts, schedules and briefing messages, plus some account setup, so written documents dominate.
length_reasoning: A small round with a few testers takes a couple of hours to script and brief; a large multi-party round with environment access takes a couple of days of active work.
review_reasoning: A QA manager reads the plan and scripts and checks that access works; larger rounds need scripts read through and coverage checked against scope.
stakes_reasoning: A poor round wastes participants' time or misses coverage, which is noticed at the round and can be rerun.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product, test environments and who the participants are, learned over weeks.

unit_flag_reason: The study can combine workflow analysis, space design and cost comparison, which are very different kinds of work, and is an unusual task for support specialists.
domain_reasoning: The work is gathering information, analysing it and writing a report with a recommendation, mostly in documents and spreadsheets-as-text.
length_reasoning: A narrow cost comparison takes a day or so; a study with workflow observation, layout and vendor quotes takes weeks of active work.
review_reasoning: Management reads the report and checks the cost figures and assumptions; a large study needs the workflow findings and sources checked.
stakes_reasoning: A flawed study can lead to buying the wrong system or a wasted spend, hard to reverse once purchased.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the office's workflows, budgets and existing systems, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into looking up product or policy information in knowledge bases and account systems.
length_reasoning: A simple question takes two minutes; a multi-part question needing lookups takes around ten.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recording at higher speed and checks the answer against the knowledge base; longer calls take proportionally longer.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong answer misleads a customer and may cause a complaint or follow-up call but can be corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's products, policies and systems, picked up over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into reading the claim or inquiry record in the case system and noting the call.
length_reasoning: A simple update call takes three minutes; explaining a denial or adjustment with questions takes up to fifteen.
review_reasoning: A QA reviewer listens to the recorded call and checks the result stated matches the case record.
stakes_reasoning: Wrongly stating a claim result or adjustment can cause complaints, disputes or regulatory exposure.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's claims process and systems and how to explain outcomes, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written note of findings and recommendations, so writing dominates once the build has been evaluated.
length_reasoning: A short note on one issue takes ten minutes; a detailed note with screenshots and steps takes an hour or so.
review_reasoning: A developer reads the note and reproduces the key points on the build; longer notes take longer to reproduce.
stakes_reasoning: Poor feedback causes misdirected fixes or missed issues that show up in later testing.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the product and its usability conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is in monitoring tools, system consoles and ticket systems.
length_reasoning: Most alerts are transient or known and closed in minutes; a real fault can take an hour or more to trace.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the closing note and glances at the graph; real faults need the reasoning and logs followed.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed alert usually recurs, but a missed real fault can become an outage.
context_reasoning: Telling noise from a real problem needs months of knowing these systems' normal behaviour.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into configuring fields, workflows and permissions in a tracker tool.
length_reasoning: Standing up a simple tracker project with default workflow takes a couple of hours; a customised one with fields, workflows, migration and onboarding takes a couple of days.
review_reasoning: A manager opens the configured project, checks the fields and workflow with test records; a complex setup needs each workflow state tried.
stakes_reasoning: A poor setup is noticed as the team uses it and can be reconfigured, with some rework of records.
context_reasoning: Needs the team's defect process and tracker conventions, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is running commands and tests on the machine and noting the result on the ticket, which is operating software and systems.
length_reasoning: A simple check after a repair takes a few minutes; verifying a complex install with several applications takes half an hour.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the ticket note and may spot-check the machine; a long verification needs the test list checked.
stakes_reasoning: A missed fault is found when the user returns and the ticket is reopened.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's standard configurations and tools, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into entering complaint details in the case or CRM system.
length_reasoning: A simple complaint takes four minutes; a complex one with background and records takes up to twenty.
review_reasoning: A reviewer listens to the call and checks that the case record captures the details.
stakes_reasoning: Missing or wrong details cause rework for the resolving staff and customer irritation, but can be recovered by contacting the customer.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's complaint process and categories, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into operating test tools and the test management tool.
length_reasoning: A small automated or short manual run takes ten minutes to trigger and log; a long manual session with many failures takes a couple of hours.
review_reasoning: A lead looks at the logged results and checks failures; long runs need failed cases checked against evidence.
stakes_reasoning: Wrongly logged results usually get caught in later runs, but a missed failure can let a bug through.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's test suites and tool setup, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The output is a written recommendation with examples, so reading contact records and writing dominate.
length_reasoning: A short recommendation with a few examples takes an hour; one backed by pulling many contacts takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A supervisor reads the recommendation and checks a few examples; a big one needs the evidence checked.
stakes_reasoning: A weak recommendation is usually declined or reworked; acting on a wrong one causes a change that can be reversed.
context_reasoning: Needs knowledge of the company's processes and who owns them, learned over months.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into working in the defect tracker, merging and editing records.
length_reasoning: A light pass on a small database takes an hour; a release-milestone pass on a large one takes most of a day.
review_reasoning: A lead spot-checks merged duplicates and statuses; a big pass needs many merges verified.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong merge or status causes confusion or missed bugs, noticed later and reversible.
context_reasoning: Judging duplicates and statuses needs deep knowledge of the product and its defect history, built over months.

domain_reasoning: The work is reading the ticket, checking systems or knowledge base, and writing a reply, which is mostly text.
length_reasoning: A routine how-to takes five minutes; a problem needing investigation and a stepwise reply takes up to forty.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the ticket and answer and checks the steps are correct.
stakes_reasoning: Wrong instructions reach the user and cause a reopened ticket, but can be corrected.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's software and standard setups, picked up over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Apart from talking, the time goes into reproducing the problem and examining logs and the application.
length_reasoning: A quick diagnosis takes fifteen minutes; a hard problem takes an hour or more on a session.
review_reasoning: A reviewer replays the recording and checks the logic and evidence for the cause; it is partly skimmable.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong cause sends the customer or field team down the wrong path, caught when the fix fails.
context_reasoning: Diagnosing needs deep knowledge of the product, its builds and known issues, built over months.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into the test environment and defect tracker, running the retest and updating the ticket.
length_reasoning: A simple fix retest takes ten minutes; one needing regression around the fix takes an hour or more.
review_reasoning: A lead reads the note and evidence; for complex fixes needs to see the regression results.
stakes_reasoning: A wrongly closed defect can ship to users, but is usually caught later and fixed.
context_reasoning: Needs the product's behaviour and the defect's history, learned over weeks.

domain_reasoning: The work is entering the request into the billing or account system and sending a confirmation.
length_reasoning: A simple change of address takes five minutes; a contract or discontinuance with checks takes about twenty-five.
review_reasoning: A colleague compares the entry against the request and checks the confirmation.
stakes_reasoning: A wrong entry can cause misbilling or service errors, often reversible but sometimes with financial effect.
context_reasoning: Needs the company's forms, systems and rules, learned over a few weeks.

domain_reasoning: Most time goes into filling vendor portals or emails with details and updating the ticket.
length_reasoning: A simple RMA takes ten minutes; a complex case with documentation and warranty checks takes an hour.
review_reasoning: A supervisor checks the case details, warranty info and ticket update.
stakes_reasoning: A mistaken referral delays the user's repair or loses warranty coverage, but is reversible.
context_reasoning: Needs the organisation's assets, warranties and vendor contacts, learned over weeks.
